blindSummary:
An international LGBT-rights mapping study (2022) examined regional regulations in eight focus states/provinces, and this state/province is not among them: the entry for this island among the eight is a differently-named jurisdiction - the one whose largest city has an enacted anti-LGBT bylaw. No enforcement incident, raid, arrest, or enacted bylaw targeting transgender people was found in the dossier here; an earlier attribution of a study finding to this jurisdiction was a misreading.

The earlier minimal-divergence flag rested on that misattributed legal-divergence note; the dossier contains no jurisdiction-level evidence that would move this state/province away from the national framework. A visitor-facing risk profile therefore follows the national picture: the new national criminal code in force from January 2026, and police extortion/arbitrary detention as its main enforcement mechanism.
blindSourceSummaries: An international LGBT-rights organisation's 2022 mapping study of national laws and regional regulations violating rights of women and LGBTIQ people: examines regional regulations in eight focus states/provinces, finding much overlap but significant regional variation (dress codes, curfews, restrictions on where transgender people may appear), and states its findings are valid beyond the focus set; this state/province is not among the eight examined.
